meta.answer:
Not on its own, I'm afraid. The BikerBed gives you a full-length small-double bed, which covers the sleeping part of the DVLA's requirements. But to change the body type to 'motor caravan', the DVLA expects all the internal features: seats and a table, sleeping accommodation, cooking facilities and storage, all rigidly fixed to the living compartment (only the table can be easily removable). They also look for external features: 2 or more windows on at least one side of the main body, a separate door into the living area, and a high-top or pop-top roof. Whether your van meets these depends on the rest of your conversion and the van itself.

If you apply, you'll need a completed conversion checklist, interior photos of each feature with the bed and table in use, exterior photos from all sides with the plates visible, and a photo of the VIN. The DVLA makes the final decision and may inspect the vehicle. It's also worth knowing that even if the body type isn't changed, you can still use the van as a camper as long as you're satisfied it meets the required internal features.
